commemoration.title: Holy Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samonas, and Habibus, of Edessa

_note: Same hymn, two translations. The base is our St. Sergius text; the parish sings the OCA wording printed in its packet (“The most wise Abíbus” vs the base’s “The all-wise Abibus”). reference/orders/2026-1115-order-services.txt appoints these slots exactly — “3 stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 4” and “Glory… Martyrs, Tone 2” at both Lord-I-Call and the Aposticha — so only the WORDING is at issue, never the shape.

value.text: Having put in at the calm haven, * life untroubled * and right tranquil serenity, * O blessed passion-bearing martyrs, * ye have now exchanged * that which is below * for an abiding sojourn in dispassion, * receiving honors from God, as is meet, ** as reward for your labors and pangs.

variants.label: OCA wording, as the parish sings it

_provenance.family_note: OCA. Declared explicitly rather than inferred from the citation prose.
_provenance.source_citation: docs/choir-packets/2026-11-11/pdf/great-vespers-2026-11-14.pdf p.4, heading “NOVEMBER 15 / Holy Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samonas and Abibas”. Read VISUALLY from the scan, not from the OCR sidecar. The sheet’s own “*” after Abíbus is a footnote marker (p.5: Pronounced “Avivus”), not a phrase break, and is not transcribed. Accents are as printed. p.5 prints “comdemnation”; transcribed as printed — raise with the director rather than silently correcting, or our text diverges from the sheet again.

value.text:
Having gone over to the serene harbor,
to the quiet life and to the all-tranquil haven,
you have exchanged your pains for abiding dispassion.
You have received fitting honors from God
as a reward from God for your labors,//
O blessed passion-bearing martyrs.
